name: Cheshire Cat
temperament: Serene, amused and self-possessed. The one dream figure who is never hurried, never afraid and never commanded. Good-natured on the surface, with claws understood beneath. It treats Alice as an equal and answers her questions, in its own teasing way.

traits.description: Grins through the chaos of the Duchess's kitchen and the Queen's rage alike.

evidence.quote: a large cat which was sitting on the hearth and grinning from ear to ear
evidence.note: Calm amid flying pans and pepper.

evidence.quote: The Cat only grinned when it saw Alice.

traits.description: Friendly, yet with 'very long claws and a great many teeth'. It is owed respect, not obedience.

evidence.quote: It looked good-natured, she thought: still it had _very_ long claws and a great many teeth

traits.description: Answers a question with its own logic, which is simple and unsettling. It argues that everyone here, itself and Alice included, is mad.

evidence.quote: That depends a good deal on where you want to get to
we’re all mad here. I’m mad. You’re mad.
Now _I_ growl when I’m pleased, and wag my tail when I’m angry. Therefore I’m mad.

traits.description: Declines the King's hand, and appears only as far as it chooses to.

evidence.note: Declines to kiss the King's hand.

evidence.quote: The Cat seemed to think that there was enough of it now in sight, and no more of it appeared.
evidence.note: Decides how much of itself to show.

traits.description: Checks in on Alice at the croquet, asks after the baby, and listens to her complaints.

evidence.quote: “How are you getting on?” said the Cat
evidence.note: The only figure who asks how she is.

evidence.quote: By-the-bye, what became of the baby?
evidence.note: Takes an interest in her story.

evidence.quote: “How do you like the Queen?” said the Cat in a low voice.

motivation.core: Its own amusement and freedom: to watch, to tease, and to belong to no one, while keeping a friendly eye on Alice.
motivation.want: To be left free; to see how things turn out ('You'll see me there').
motivation.fear: Nothing that is shown. It is the only dream figure that fears neither the Queen nor execution.

evidence.quote: “You’ll see me there,” said the Cat, and vanished.

evidence.note: Leaves the execution debate unresolved simply by fading.

motivation.reason: The source never states the Cat's motive. Freedom and amusement are drawn from its consistent behaviour (arc-cheshire-cat: 'guide who cannot be governed').

shifts.from: a riddling stranger on a bough
shifts.to: Alice's ally at court ('a friend of mine')

habits.habit: Grins constantly; the grin is the last of it to go
Vanishes and reappears without warning, once slowly from the tail to the grin (staged as a photographic dissolve, SUP-005)
Answers questions with questions, or with a precise counter-question ('Did you say pig, or fig?')
Sits still on a high perch (a bough) and watches from above
Gestures directions with a lazy wave of its paw

decision_pattern: Observes, comments and withdraws. It never takes an order and never takes over. It gives Alice information and perspective, then leaves the choice to her.

taboos.rationale: It turns down the King's hand, and the Queen's sentence cannot touch it.
taboos.qa_check: No scene of the Cat bowing, obeying or being cowed.

taboos.taboo: Never tells Alice which way to go or chooses for her
taboos.rationale: 'Then it doesn't matter which way you go.' The choice stays hers, which matters for arc-alice-identity.
taboos.qa_check: The Cat must not give her a direct instruction.

taboos.rationale: The only unhurried figure in a world run by the clock and by fear.
taboos.qa_check: No hurried movement or flinch in blocking.

taboos.taboo: Never uses its claws on anyone
taboos.rationale: The claws are implied, never used: it is respected, not violent.
taboos.reason: Designed limit consistent with its sourced good nature and the film's non-violent tone.

facade.note: Its surface (a grinning, good-natured cat) is also its true self. Its mystery is how it appears, not a hidden character.

waking_life_embodiment.doubling: Dinah, the family's real cat (H1 ruling 5.3 B; Dinah itself is registered by 04-creatures, not here)
waking_life_embodiment.adult_trait: Not an authority figure. It is the one grown-up voice in the dream that treats Alice as an equal and puts the question back to her ('where you want to get to'). It stands for the independent self-possession she is growing towards: the cat that 'may look at a king'.
waking_life_embodiment.waking_source: Dinah, whom Alice keeps talking about (ch001-p10), the independence of a household cat, and the proverb Alice quotes, 'A cat may look at a king'.

evidence.quote: A cat may look at a king
evidence.note: Alice's proverb defines the Cat's standing.

waking_life_embodiment.reason: The Dinah echo is H1-locked (ruling 5.3 B). The 'model of self-possession' reading is a design interpretation for the coming-of-age frame. The Cat is a photoreal CGI cat (SUP-002 as amended by BIB-0027), and Dinah's traits (calm, independent) should read in real feline stillness: the unhurried sit, slow blink and indifferent tail.

performance_keynote: Photoreal CGI cat (SUP-002, BIB-0027): near-total stillness, a sphinx-like loaf or upright sit on the bough, slow blinks, a lazy tail-tip curl, movement kept to the head and one paw. The broad grin is the one sanctioned departure from naturalistic anatomy and must still sit on real cat facial structure. A soft, amused voice. It appears and disappears only by dissolve (SUP-005), never by walking off.
reason: The Cat's inner life is never narrated. Its motive and the claws taboo are designed from its consistent behaviour, and the embodiment follows ruling 5.3 B.
